finding.current_runtime_behavior: play_start() records started_ns immediately after Popen(paplay). The cancel offset is later computed as cancel_request_ns - that process-spawn timestamp.
finding.current_analyzer_behavior: The analyzer converts cancel_offset_ms directly to cancel_frame on the source waveform and subtracts the same value from the last source-correlated source-timeline frame to report cancel-to-last-old-audio tail.
finding.existing_alignment_is_insufficient: Source-to-control and source-to-cancel monitor FFT alignment proves waveform identity/offset inside captured PCM, but it does not bind the monotonic Popen timestamp to source frame 0 or to the first sample actually queued/processed/presented by the playback stream.
finding.causal_problem: Client startup, Pulse/PipeWire queuing, conversion and graph delay can shift source-frame timeline relative to process-spawn monotonic time. The current arithmetic can therefore classify the wrong source windows as post-cancel or mismeasure cancel-to-last-old-audio tail.

external_primary_refresh.observed: PipeWire exposes pw_stream_get_time_n() with graph ticks, delay, queued and buffered data; total playback delay includes application queued data, resampler buffering and graph/device delay.
PipeWire Pulse emulation has independent playback buffering controls including request and target-length defaults, so client process start is not an audio-position identity.
PipeWire documents stream latency as time for a sample to travel from application to playback target, reinforcing that process launch and target presentation are distinct boundaries.

counterhypothesis.statement: The fixed 150 ms startup wait makes Popen time close enough to source frame 0 for this test.
counterhypothesis.reason: A sleep can reduce startup races but provides no measured mapping from monotonic cancel time to source-frame position. PipeWire exposes explicit stream timing precisely because queue/buffer/graph delay are separate quantities.

minimal_trigger4_repair.goal: Bind the promotion-bearing cancel instant to an observed playback/source timeline rather than process-spawn time while preserving the existing VoicePacketCortex cancellation authority.
preferred_shape: Do not interpret paplay Popen timestamp as source-frame-0 identity for terminal tail measurement.

Use an existing or minimal read-only/native PipeWire playback timing surface that can report stream ticks/source position plus queued/buffered/delay at or immediately before the causal cancel; pw_stream_get_time_n() is the primary documented timing primitive.
Persist the exact mapping from cancel monotonic timestamp to source-frame/source-timeline position and its stream/node identity in the evidence receipt.

If a causal mapping cannot be observed on the selected client surface, fail closed as EVIDENCE_INVALID_CANCEL_SOURCE_TIMELINE_UNBOUND; do not infer PRODUCT_NEGATIVE from source-frame windows derived from Popen time.
Keep source/control/cancel PCM alignment as an independent waveform/readback validity check; do not replace it with timing self-report alone.
required_regressions: Inject or simulate different playback-client startup delays with identical stream/sample progression: measured cancel source position must remain bound to stream/sample timing rather than shift with Popen delay.
Missing stream/source-position timing with otherwise green PCM correlation must prevent terminal G2 completeness.
Cancel source-frame mapping must identify the same exact playback stream/object lineage used by the G2 PipeWire evidence.
Existing H4, Piper-runtime identity, predeclared latency-bound, replacement readback, packet fence, cleanup-evidence and zero-credit fences remain intact.

execution_fence.next_action: Trigger4 folds this source-timeline binding into the same current G2 validity repair descendant, proves focused regressions, then one fresh exact repaired S2 subject may run if singleton ownership is clear.
